summary: Long Seridan Airport (ODN) is a small rural airstrip serving the remote community of Long Seridan in the interior of Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo. It provides vital air access to one of the most isolated regions of Borneo, connecting the local Penan and other indigenous communities to larger urban centers. The airport primarily handles short-haul turboprop flights operated by Malaysia's rural air service providers.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Long Seridan Airport?
A: MASwings (a subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines) operates turboprop services to Long Seridan, typically using ATR aircraft on routes connecting to other rural Sarawak airstrips and Miri.

Q: Is Long Seridan Airport suitable for large aircraft?
A: No, the airport has a short runway and is designed to handle small turboprop aircraft suited for short take-off and landing operations in remote terrain.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport terminal?
A: The terminal is very basic, reflecting the airport's small size. Passengers should expect minimal amenities and limited services.

Q: Can I book flights to Long Seridan online?
A: Flights to Long Seridan can typically be booked through the Malaysia Airlines/MASwings website or through travel agents specializing in rural Borneo travel.
transport_tips: There is no public bus service to the airport; the most common way to reach it is by 4WD vehicle along logging tracks and dirt roads that can take several hours from the nearest town. Most travelers arrive by air since road access is limited and conditions can be difficult, especially during the rainy season. Arranging transport directly with a local guesthouse or tour operator in advance is recommended.
local_tip: Pack light and bring a small daypack with essentials in your carry-on—checked baggage occasionally takes extra time to arrive at this remote strip, and weather delays are common during the monsoon months from November to February.
